changed.what: Convention 14 applied: 'A run verb has no scope input' and 'the same command started directly is refused' were false under NJL-01. An implementer would have built a scope order with no citation and refused every agent over MCP above E0. Now the bead has the six common run inputs and Demand.scope = token, then cited envelope_scope, then derived scope, then adhoc. A cited scope with no approved row is E0. Token case 4: a contradicting citation is 761 with pointer /envelope_scope, observed the cited scope, required the token's, with the row's two repairs. Repair (3) ends 'resubmit citing --envelope-scope'. The OPEN is dropped. Added the tests citation_contradicting_token_is_761, cited_scope_admitted and scope_order, and script steps: a direct cited run is admitted with one meter row under the cited scope; an adhoc citation is 802; a contradicting citation under frob-launch is refused. needed_class had no answer for an adhoc demand, which is every request sim.estimate prices. A two-device estimate would have read 'above every class', telling an agent that nothing can be requested. It now gives the smallest class whose per-run limits contain the demand, with admitted_by none, and needed_class_cases covers it. Conventions 7 and 8: the script called M2 verbs it does not depend on, and at M0 'frob sim run @fixture:envelope-two-device' is 724, so step 3 could never pass. It now uses BD-024's M0 sim.run (BD-024 added to deps) and names the later beads that assert the M2 refusals. The acceptance parenthetical promised that sim.estimate prints E1 for a two-device demand, which no sim verb can express; it now points to BD-219, N36-32 and N36-08. Admission step 1 now says where a run verb's demand comes from before BD-219's model exists. Took item 6 of N34-15 (guard and admission agree on one shared fixture; the test guard_and_admission_agree) and added N34-15 to deps. C13 narration ('empty until BD-219 registers', 'skipped here until the classifier exists', 'earlier text of this bead') restated as fact.

Step 8 recorded 'the M0 part' with no command, so no session knew how or who records it. Now: the record_gate command with --part M0, on the receipt N36-29 prints, run by a non-implementing session (N38b-19). Step 2 now cites envelope row R1 (E1 for gate:GATE-SPARK-21, frob-launch --request R1, and R1's fallback when it is not approved). Test planning_value_replaced asserted that the target register returns 'the measured value with status tolerance'. That is not what N36-01's threshold returns (0.67 x the measured rate, after the interim floor), so the test is restated against N36-01's incumbent reference and threshold.

Report rule 2 narrated 'until the registry assigns' and lacked the detail. Now it is 862 with detail rates-violate-unit-ordering and pointer rates.ordering, through N36-03's check_ordering and constants (N36-REF; N35-33 rule 7), with the test validate_ordering_detail. Took the N36-01 audit item: a point estimate for a ratio row is refused with 863, mapped here from the typed error of N36-01's judge (rule 4, an acceptance item, the test ratio_row_refuses_point_estimate); N36-01 cannot build 863 without N35-REF. The one-meter-row paragraph said admit_run 'has no scope flag'; restated under convention 14.

Added deps N34-17 (the core's JSON reader, which the schema test parses with; frob-core has no JSON library) and STD-TEST (the property runner of frob_core::testkit). The ordering paragraph narrated 'until the refusal registry assigns one'. It now states the interim (862, detail rates-violate-unit-ordering, pointer rates.ordering, a held ledger request) with the two named constants. N36-13 and BD-216 raise it from this module's typed errors, because this module may not depend on N35-REF without pushing N36-01 and its dependents ten layers later. The H record used ';' separators, which is not TOML, so an implementer copying it gets a parse error; rewritten one key per line. Added dep N34-18 (WorkloadId = BLAKE3 over CanonicalBytes). The acceptance item 'the loader is used by the parity-baseline script and the target register' checked two later beads (convention 7); it now checks the one API this bead exposes. 'it is asked to call this function' (N16a-14 does call it) and 'correcting an earlier draft' restated as facts.

BD-029 moved to related. The audit holds: frob-core cannot name frob-kernels' type, the check compares a supplied digest, and the fixtures are synthetic. Step 4 now runs check_ordering on the block's rates and raises the ordering interim (862, detail, pointer rates.ordering) that N35-REF's row lists as a trigger of 862 for a block. Preflight called 'frob spark fingerprint --json' with no --device and no --key, both of which VERBS-spark requires, and a fresh fingerprint cannot test currency. It now calls 'frob spark devices --json' (N21c-04, added to deps), then 'frob spark fingerprint --device <d> --soak 20m --key pb-fp-<run-id>-<d> --json' for each stale or missing device, one job per card on trj (R11's E0 form).

Considerations said that N21a-27, N38a-08 and N38a-07 name the entry point frob_core::perf::ceiling and that 'the correction is requested'. All three already use frob_conformance::perf::bound::ceiling, so the sentence sent an implementer looking for a rename that does not exist. Now stated as fact.

The budget said two strong campaigns and the weak campaign fit the 12 device-hours of E1. It omitted the A/A control (about 3.4) and the lever campaigns of the optimization pass (about 3.6 each on the two-card row). About 9.8 device-hours are spent before the pass, so one lever would exhaust the never-reset meter, and the post-pass campaign that decides KILL-SHARD would be refused (761, device_hours). The budget is recomputed in full, with a rule: a lever campaign starts only if it and the post-pass campaign fit the remainder, otherwise it is ledgered rejected(budget); tests budget_estimate and post_pass_reserved. The bead also had to 'record' the scaling clause of GATE-CORTEX-08, which N23a-19 records and which N40-02 enters as Parity with 'the scaling figure is evaluated by GATE-SPARK-20'. That made two recorders of one gate (convention 9). It now states that GATE-SPARK-20's record carries the clause and that no second CORTEX-08 record is written. The script section named a step 'strong_post' that N36-31 does not have; it now names the pre and post phases and their steps.

Applied F-U23b. Start is now gated on the KILL-ALTALGO entry for algorithm:async-sharding reading not-fired, not 'funded', which no record holds. The pilot is PILOT-ALTALGO-06 withdrawn with reason 'not run: sharding stopped', not 'not-run'. start_checks_both_gates is rewritten with the N40-03 outcomes; it waited for 'killed'/'not-funded'. The frob-launch parenthetical said only the launcher token gives a run verb a scope; restated under convention 14.

The acceptance item said a two-shard job started directly is always adhoc and refused. Under convention 14, a direct start citing --envelope-scope gate:GATE-SPARK-20 is admitted. The 761 two-shard item had no test; added two_shard_job_under_e0_is_761, which is where N36-20 now points for the train.start refusal.

The lanes step submitted '--key lane-<s>' and compared against solo runs whose keys were not given. A solo run with the same key and request returns the concurrent job's stored receipt, so the digest comparison could never fail, and a re-run of the script submitted nothing. Keys now carry the run id, and solo runs have their own keys.

The order at admission named 602, 761 and session budgets, without the daemon's 704 between 602 and 761 or the code 701 (convention 14), so the fit slot's implementer would have mis-ordered the daemon path. Took N36-19's half of item 5 per the audit: N36-19 cannot test the time estimate, because it does not depend on N36-17. Added an acceptance item and the test bins_change_time_not_bytes (bins change the time group, not the memory group); request to N36-17 for the ray work in its JobShape. The record's envelope {needed, in_force} did not say for which scope, so an agent could not tell why in_force reads E0 after an approval. It now says: sim.estimate, a read verb with no envelope_scope, prices under adhoc, and a run verb's --estimate prices under the scope the run would carry. Added the test adhoc_prices_by_limits, using a memory-bound request, because no sim request places one job on two devices. 'about 5.8 M worlds of Q' is 203.3e9 / 34,556 = 5.88 M, so it now reads 5.9 M, and the mac_budget test prints it. Checked the N16c-15 counterpart: the edge N16c-15 -> BD-219 is the right direction, and nothing is needed here.

Acceptance item 1 required the fourth clause of GATE-SPARK-22 to be recorded for Q and H on each device. That is N36-32's assembly and N36p1-01's recording, and both depend on this bead (convention 7), so the item could not be closed here. It now states the figure this bead shows and who assembles and records the clause. Background said 10^5 operations at 20% of 8.3e13 allows 165 M world-steps/s; it is 166 M, which is what the test arithmetic_is_not_the_bound asserts.

Applied H-owners-2 (R28). Row 9 was sized to the 12 device-hours of a gate measurement, which no row can admit for a row with no gate: four pairs, and the row never judged. The bead now files R28 before the first pair with N21c-35's fields as N44-01 shows them: admits campaign:perf-row9-humanoid; class E2; limits equal to E2's, because N44-01's lint rows_limits_equal_class_limits refuses other limits; the 25 device-hour estimate in its scope prose; and the not-approved fallback 'not run, no ratio'. Ten pairs are declared and must fit the limit before any arm, and every two-card arm runs under frob-launch --scope campaign:perf-row9-humanoid --request R28. Tests row9_pairs_fit_budget and r28_row_fields; acceptance updated. The row-16 command carried nothing that distinguishes the three scenarios (standing, walking, push recovery), so the 30 runs were one request and the 'minimum over scenarios' measured nothing; it now passes --task. Keys carry the seed, since another seed under the same key is 803. The frob-launch parenthetical is restated under convention 14. Request to WP-47.

The restate function's rules covered 18 of the 22 target rows. Rows 15, 16, 17 and 22 had no rule, while step 3 restates 'all 22 rows' and the acceptance exercises the whole table, so an implementer had to invent behaviour or drop rows. Added rule 6 for those rows (row 15's unit line takes d_new; 16 and 22 are unchanged; 17's ratios are unchanged) and the test every_row_has_a_rule.

The acceptance asked the KILL-PARITY register row to cite 'the commit, the command, its output'. Those are fields of a measurement gate's part. The item now states that entry and the read-only kill_gate_records.sh --live check. The decide step ran 'cargo test --test g2_parity -- KILL-PARITY (the tier target of the gate's record)', but a kill row has no tier and the tier runner selects only by gate, row, site or milestone (BD-025), so it ran nothing. It now runs an example target kill_parity that this bead declares.

Same defects as N36-27, for KILL-SHARD. The acceptance cited 'commit, command, output' on the kill row instead of N40-03's decision entry. The decision function ran as '--test g2_parity -- KILL-SHARD (the tier target of the gate's record)' although kill rows have no tier. It now runs an example kill_shard and the kill_gate_records.sh --live check.

Preflight called 'frob spark fingerprint --json' without --device and --key, which VERBS-spark requires; a fresh run cannot test currency either. It now calls 'frob spark devices --json' and stops with the fingerprint repair printed, inside the 45-minute budget. The ordering rejection of step 2 now asserts the detail rates-violate-unit-ordering.

The envelope paragraph said 'A run verb has no scope input', which is false under convention 14; restated, keeping frob-launch because step 5's arm is two commands. Preflight 'frob spark fingerprint --json' got the same fix as N36-29. The keys of the equivalence, strong and quality steps had no phase, and a pair's request is identical in pre and post. The post-pass strong campaign, which KILL-SHARD reads, would therefore have returned the pre-pass receipts and measured nothing. Keys now carry the phase and the seed. The A/A step gave no keys, so a repeated one-card job under one key passes vacuously; each run now has its own key. The weak and A/A campaigns ran in both phases, adding about 3.9 device-hours to R2's never-reset 12, so the post-pass strong campaign would be refused (761). They now run in pre only, and the post receipt cites them, matching BD-199's budget.

Preflight 'frob spark fingerprint --json' got the same fix as N36-29. The capacity step cited '<the row N36p1-01 cites>' and 'a run verb started directly has scope adhoc'. It now cites R1, which per N44-01 admits gate:GATE-SPARK-22, and convention 14. Step envelope_class asked sim verbs to price and submit a two-device job, but sim.run and sim.estimate place one job on one device, so the step could never pass. It now uses a memory-bound request on the Mac (1,000,000 Q worlds, 34.6 GB, pointer memory) and a 24-worker request (pointer cores), each estimated (E1, in force E0) and refused with 761, and leaves the two-device case to N36-08. Added BD-160, the owner of --workers, to deps (convention 8). Took N36-19's item 3 per the audit: the camera points at 1, 8, 64 and 256 worlds, with an acceptance item and BD-188 in deps.

The C13 finding holds: '(the dependency requested of N21a-27 and BD-214 missing)' narrated a request, and both beads already depend on this one (checked); restated as fact. requests.what: Drop acceptance item 6 (the guard and N36-20's admission give the same verdict on one shared scratch fixture). N36-20 now holds it as an acceptance item and the test guard_and_admission_agree, and depends on N34-15; this resolves the audit's wrong-way edge.

Drop acceptance item 5 and the test ratio_row_refuses_point_estimate. judge takes N36-06's paired-bound type and returns a typed error for a point estimate on a ratio_* row, with no refusal code. BD-216 now maps it to FROB-REF-863 and carries the item and the test.

(1) Matrix row 862: the rate-schema site (missing decimation) and the ordering-interim site are N36-13 (a block's rates, check step 4) and BD-216 (report rules 1 and 2). Both raise it from N36-03's typed errors and its named constants ORDERING_DETAIL and ORDERING_POINTER; N36-03 builds no code. Row 863: add BD-216's mapping of the typed error of N36-01's judge. (2) The 761 script step 'frob sim run @fixture:envelope-two-device' names a request no sim.run input expresses: --tier places one job on one device, and the positional is a design. Use a memory-bound request on the Mac (--workload Q --tier batch-cpu --worlds 1000000, 34.6 GB, pointer memory) or a 24-worker request (--workers 24, pointer cores), as N36-32's step envelope_class does. (3) The 602 step's Mac case ('the same with --tier gpu-metal'): 200,000 H worlds (19.3 GB) fit the Mac's 203.3 GB budget, so the Mac gives 761 (above E0's 16 GiB), not 602. A world count above the budget is needed, for example 2,200,000 H worlds (212.7 GB). (4) '--test g1_known_answers -- refusals::perf' is a name filter, but the tier runner selects only by gate, row, site or milestone (BD-025), so it runs nothing. Use the KA rows' ids or a declared check target.

Its test plan says the submission path (frob sim estimate @fixture:two-card-train; frob train start @fixture:two-card-train --key em-train) is a step of N36-20's script. Row R2 (E1, 12 device-hours for gate:GATE-SPARK-20): at incumbent-like times BD-199 spends about 9.8 device-hours before its optimization pass (two strong campaigns 5.9, A/A control 3.4, weak 0.5), leaving about 2.2 against about 3.6 per lever campaign on the two-card row. The owner may wish to size R2, or admit a campaign scope for the pass.

Audit counterpart (this bead is in no round-4 slice). N36-32 now carries acceptance item 3 (a camera task's measured high-water mark within 5% at 1, 8, 64 and 256 worlds, step cameras) and depends on BD-188. BD-219 now carries the time half of item 5 (bins change the time estimate, test bins_change_time_not_bytes), which N36-19 cannot test because it does not depend on N36-17. Drop item 3 and the time half of item 5, keeping 'not the byte estimate'. Then move BD-188 to related if nothing else in the bead needs it.

BD-219's test bins_change_time_not_bytes hands the time model a job shape that differs by the camera's ray work times its exposure or rolling-shutter bins (N36-19's b). N36-17's JobShape and y-hat carry no sensor ray work, so the bins cannot change the time interval. Add the ray-work term (rays per world-step, times bins) to JobShape and its stratum, or name the term that carries it.

Script step 6 expects 'frob --registries-root <scratch> sim estimate @fixture:two-card-train' to print class in force E1 after the E1 row is approved in the scratch registry. sim.estimate is a read verb with no envelope_scope, so it prices under adhoc, where the class in force is E0 whatever is approved (BD-219, N36-20, convention 14). No sim verb expresses a two-card training either. To show a scratch approval changing the class in force, use a run verb's --estimate citing the approved scope with --envelope-scope.

Acceptance item on GATE-CORTEX-08 says 'the scaling clause is BD-199's'. BD-199 now writes no GATE-CORTEX-08 record (convention 9: one recorder). The scaling clause is evaluated by GATE-SPARK-20's record, as N40-02 enters the gate ('the scaling figure is evaluated by GATE-SPARK-20 and KILL-SHARD'), and N23a-19's record_gate is the only recording of GATE-CORTEX-08. State that in place of 'is BD-199's'.

BD-216 took N36-01's item 5. The N36-19 counterparts were taken by BD-219 and N36-32, with a request to N36-19, which no round-4 slice reviews. The N16c-15 counterpart for BD-219 needed nothing. N36-06 needs nothing; BD-216 takes the item. F-U34's request that N36-20 depend on N34p3-01 was not applied, because the script no longer passes @fixture: references at M0; BD-024 was added instead. N36-06's A/A arithmetic was re-simulated: 26% of 3%-biased campaigns clear 1.02, and P(X<=9) = 0.972 at 5%, 0.055 at 15%, 1.8e-5 at 26%. N36-16's dense, band, lattice and capacity figures were recomputed and all hold. Left as is: N36-16 and N36-18 describe their end-to-end coverage as steps of N36-32's script rather than scripts of their own (the round-3 form for library models whose verb lands later). No cycles after the edits (graph_check cycles = 0). Every touched file parses (front matter, one-line JSON lists, seven sections), checked with a script in the scratchpad.
